## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
Every earlier trial scored 0, including the training success, across many heads, trunks and recipe settings. That points to a learning-dynamics failure that does not depend on the architecture, not to weak features. One likely cause is collapse onto DONE. Under a random policy most placements add extra cells and get negative reward, while DONE ends the episode at 0. DONE is a single action that collects all of that positive advantage, so the policy may learn to stop before it learns where to place. In that case it stops collecting placement data and never recovers. This round tests that idea in two ways: (1) slowing how fast the DONE logit can learn, using a constant output scale, and (2) a recipe region nobody has tried (8 PPO epochs, higher entropy, smaller batches) that reuses each placement sample more. A third candidate combines both with a column-skip head. If all three stay at 0, the cause is probably something else.

### Round 2
Every trial so far, here and in the earlier search, scores exactly 0 on dev and also 0 on training success. That covers about 15 architectures and recipes, so nothing can be ranked. A simple policy should already get some designs right: put a 1x1 brick on any column whose next cell up is in the target and still missing. A per-column 1x1 stem could learn that from the dense reward. Since nothing learned it, something basic may differ from the task description, possibly one of the hidden quirks the note warns about. One candidate quirk is how actions are numbered. Our convolutional heads assume type-major, y-major numbering with each brick's top-left cell as its anchor. If the world numbers actions differently, these heads cannot learn the mapping. Fully flat heads could learn it, but they may learn too slowly. So I test a head that allows for several possible numberings and footprint anchors and learns which one fits. I also try an untried recipe region and the two combined.

### Round 3
After 18 trials across two searches (6 here, 12 before), nothing has scored above 0.000, on dev or in training. The trials covered conv, transformer and MLP networks, with heads that assume the action layout and heads that don't, plus many recipes. The task's own check expects a normal world to reach up to 25% exact builds after only 8,192 steps, so learning itself must be blocked. The most likely cause is a quirk in the world, not a lack of capacity. The best-supported guess is a spatial mismatch between the observation grid and the action numbering. A conv head can't learn a flip of that kind, and the flat heads may be too slow to learn it within this budget. Our earlier hedge covered transposes, bottom-right anchors and cell-major numbering, but not flips. So two candidates test a local head that hedges all 8 flip/transpose frames and both numbering orders, under two different recipes. The third tests the untried low learning rate with a long horizon on the starting network.

### Round 4
All 9 trials in this search scored exactly 0, as did the 12 trials in the earlier search, on both training and dev. The failure is in learning itself. The following made no difference: changes to the recipe (epochs 1-8, lr 3e-4 to 2e-3, entropy 0-0.02, gamma 0.9-0.99, clip 0.3, 64-512 envs), action-layout hedging, and a slowed DONE logit. Two causes remain untested. First, early collapse onto DONE: random placements earn negative reward, so stopping straight away looks good, and the single shared DONE logit gets a far more consistent gradient than any one of about 200 placements. Scaling the DONE logit by 0.2 only slowed this down; it did not give a strong prior against stopping. Second, optimisation problems inside the network: the standard PPO setup (orthogonal init, near-uniform policy output, separate critic so value gradients don't disturb the policy features, normalisation) has never been tried. This is the last round, so I test each fix alone and then both together.
